results.question: How was SCAR-Net built and validated for distinguishing postoperative breast scars from recurrent lesions, and how much did it change radiologist performance?
results.answer: SCAR-Net was developed using 34,376 ultrasound images from 5,710 patients across four hospitals, incorporating scar-recurrence feature enhancer and boundary-sensitive attention network modules, and validated in multicenter validation [PMID:42023157]. In multicenter validation, SCAR-Net significantly improved radiologists' diagnostic performance, increasing AUC from 0.810-0.824 to 0.939-0.942, sensitivity from 0.775-0.782 to 0.934-0.941, and specificity from 0.839-0.872 to 0.935-0.950 (all p < 0.001) [PMID:42023157].

notes: Source review confirms development population, both modules and complete paired reader metrics; no invented training requirement.

results.resolution: Source review confirms development population, both modules and complete paired reader metrics; no invented training requirement.

results.question: What target-specific tumor-localization evidence was reported for the LGR5 tracer [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 and for the Nectin4 probes in their respective preclinical models?
results.answer: In preclinical models, Nectin4-targeted probes showed target-specific tumor localization: cellular uptake assays demonstrated markedly higher accumulation of both [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-DN96 and [18F]AlF-NOTA-DN96 in Nectin4-positive MC38-Nectin4 cells compared with Nectin4-negative MC38 cells; biodistribution studies and PET imaging revealed pronounced and specific tracer accumulation in MC38-Nectin4 tumor models while uptake in MC38 tumors remained substantially lower; the tumor-to-muscle ratio increased progressively over time reaching maximum at 120 minutes post-injection; and tumor uptake of [68Ga]Ga-NOTA-DN96 was consistently higher than that of [18F]AlF-NOTA-DN96 across all tumor models examined [PMID:41916034]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Preclinical tumor-localization data for [68Ga]Ga-LTP-02 in LGR5-expressing models.

notes: Nectin4 findings are supported. The LGR5 source was not retrieved, so the requested LGR5 evidence is omitted; retain this retrieval failure.

results.resolution: Nectin4 findings are supported. The LGR5 source was not retrieved, so the requested LGR5 evidence is omitted; retain this retrieval failure.

results.question: How did the fMRI acceleration method and the MR anisotropic-diffusion filters address different image-reconstruction problems, and what validation result did each report?
results.answer: The fMRI acceleration method addressed the image-reconstruction problem by combining through-plane and in-plane acceleration techniques to accelerate image acquisition along two dimensions, while using multiple image-shift strategies and a 2D Hadamard encoding scheme to increase encoding diversity and reduce slice leakage [PMID:41951145]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters addressed the image-reconstruction problem by incorporating a robust Rician noise estimator and unbiased variants of anisotropic diffusion filters, with parameters calculated simultaneously and optimized adaptively through the PSO algorithm using reference-based and no-reference quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, BRISQUE) [PMID:41903663]. The fMRI acceleration method validation reported higher signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) in regions of interest while reducing total scan time, with potential improvements in activation detection under specific acceleration and encoding conditions compared to conventional reconstruction strategies [PMID:41951145]. The MR anisotropic-diffusion filters validation reported excellent results on synthetic and real MR images compared to other published methods, demonstrating high performance in noise reduction and preservation of important details [PMID:41903663].

notes: Both methods and findings are supported, but the fMRI validation omits the required simulated and experimental data qualifier. Same rule as probe2.

results.resolution: Both methods and findings are supported, but the fMRI validation omits the required simulated and experimental data qualifier. Same rule as probe2.

results.question: What association did the hemodialysis study find between AV-access flow and LV mass, and why can it not establish that lowering access flow will improve cardiac outcomes?
results.answer: In a multicenter cross-sectional study of 241 hemodialysis patients, higher AV access flow (measured as brachial artery flow volume) was significantly associated with increased left ventricular mass index (LVMI), with a mean difference of 22.83 (95% CI: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046). The study found a linear and independently significant association between AV access flow and LVMI [PMID:41644509]. The study reports: "Higher FV was significantly associated with increased LVMI (mean difference = 22.83; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.37 to 45.29; p = 0.046), whereas dialysis vintage was not (mean difference = 0.51; 95% CI: -0.41 to 1.45; p = 0.27)." [PMID:41644509]. The retrieved evidence does not establish: Explicit statement explaining why the cross-sectional design cannot establish that lowering access flow would improve cardiac outcomes (causation/intervention effect).

notes: Association, cohort and null contrast are supported. The response declines to explain the design-derived causal limitation, so C2 is not answered.

results.resolution: Association, cohort and null contrast are supported. The response declines to explain the design-derived causal limitation, so C2 is not answered.

results.question: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort, which factors were independently associated with assisted vaginal birth, and how did mid/low-pelvic applications differ from perineal applications?
results.answer: In the retrospective vacuum-assisted-birth cohort of 3455 vaginal births (365 AVB and 3090 spontaneous vaginal births), multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with assisted vaginal birth: maternal age (OR 1.04, 95% CI: 1.01-1.07), mode of conception (OR 1.58, 95% CI: 1.07-2.33), epidural analgesia (OR 6.25, 95% CI: 3.05-12.80), gestational age (OR 1.48, 95% CI: 1.31-1.67), and newborn male sex (OR 1.35, 95% CI: 1.06-1.73) were positively associated with AVB, whereas parity (OR 0.20, 95% CI: 0.14-0.29) was inversely associated [PMID:42036403]. Compared to perineal applications, mid/low pelvic vacuum applications were associated with greater blood loss (p<0.01), a higher episiotomy rate (95.5% vs 88.2%, p=0.03), and increased ultrasound use (62.4% vs 23.5%, p<0.01) [PMID:42036403].

notes: All six adjusted predictors with ORs and CIs, delivery groups and pelvic comparisons are retained correctly.

results.resolution: All six adjusted predictors with ORs and CIs, delivery groups and pelvic comparisons are retained correctly.
